task.description: Idiom/scope hard gate on ISSUE-FIXER's fix for ISS-0412 (fetch_rule_commit_timestamp/0's blind DateTime.from_iso8601 |> elem(1)) before TEST-DESIGNER.

result.summary: Verified diff independently via `git diff cb72010e..HEAD -- lib/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs.ex`: it is exactly the claimed single hunk in fetch_rule_commit_timestamp/0 (lines 641-654), replacing `out |> String.trim() |> DateTime.from_iso8601() |> elem(1)` with an explicit `case ... {:ok, ts, _offset} -> ts; {:error, _reason} -> nil end`. No other file touched, no unrelated edits, no new public API, no new abstraction -- this is the minimal, structurally correct fix, not a crutch. Idiom check: this is a Mix task (tooling script), not gen_statem/OTP application code, so the gen_statem-vs-GenServer and InstanceSupervisor isolation questions (review checklist items 1-2) do not apply to this file; nothing here touches supervision or process architecture. Read the caller chain myself (created_at_after_rule?/1 at line 618-627 and rule_commit_timestamp/0 at 629-639): created_at_after_rule?/1 already has `floor when not is_nil(floor) <- rule_commit_timestamp()` in its `with`, falling through to its `else _ -> false` clause on nil -- i.e. nil is an already-established, correct 'floor unavailable, skip the advisory WARN' sentinel, used identically by the pre-existing git-exit-failure branch (the `_ -> nil` two lines below the fix). The fix makes the parse-failure path structurally identical to that already-correct sibling path; it does not invent a new sentinel or new failure semantics. Checked whether {:error, reason} could mean something more serious than 'reparse this value': DateTime.from_iso8601/1's only error reasons (:invalid_format, :invalid_date, :invalid_time, :missing_offset) are all string-parsing failures of the git output already captured on a successful (exit 0) git invocation -- there is no wrong-git-invocation or wrong-commit class of error reachable through this branch; a bad git invocation is already exhaustively handled by the `{out, 0} -> ... ; _ -> nil` match on System.cmd's own exit status. Confirmed by inspection this is the sole distinguishing branch and no error class is being silently upgraded to 'ignore' that should instead surface. Scope: single file, single function, no new named functions, no behaviour/macro/generic plumbing added -- not scope creep. Consistency: grepped test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs for fetch_rule_commit_timestamp/created_at_after_rule?/ARTIFACTS_OUT_SELF_REF/self_ref -- zero matches; no existing test exercises this code path today, so no existing assertion needed to change, consistent with ISSUE-FIXER's 'no test file changes' claim. Independently ran (foreground, this session, not trusting ISSUE-FIXER's prior claims): `mix compile --warnings-as-errors` after touching the file to force recompilation -- exit 0, zero output (clean, no warnings). `mix format --check-formatted` -- exit 0, zero output (already formatted). `mix test test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs` -- 'Result: 22 passed', exit 0, zero failures. `git status --short` after the compile touch showed no diff (mtime-only, content unchanged) -- confirms I reviewed the actual committed fix, not a modified working tree. Acceptance-criteria check against docs/issues/ISS-0412.yaml: this issue file has no separate `acceptance_criteria:` key (that field name doesn't exist in this issue's schema); its `description:` field states the fix requirement in prose ('add proper error handling around DateTime.from_iso8601/1's result instead of blind elem(1) extraction') -- satisfied verbatim by the diff. The concurrency repro ISSUE-FIXER ran (TEST_PARALLEL_N=16 scripts/test_parallel.sh, 3x, all runs 3055/3057 passed with the 2 failures being a pre-existing, unrelated, environment-only rustc :enoent gap in Mix.Tasks.Letflow.CheckToolchainTest, zero lint_handoffs/DateTime failures across 48 partition-runs) is accepted at face value per this task's instructions (not independently re-run, wall-clock cost) but the report's own content -- identical failure signature and identical unrelated file/module across all 3 runs, explicit stacktrace confirmation it never touches lint_handoffs.ex -- is internally consistent and plausible, not just asserted. Verdict: PASS. TEST-DESIGNER routing call: no new test and no refactor-for-testability is warranted here. fetch_rule_commit_timestamp/0 is a private helper inside a Mix task (tooling, not core domain/OTP logic), the fix is a 4-line mechanical case-match whose correctness is verifiable by inspection (exhaustively matches DateTime.from_iso8601/1's only two return shapes), and extracting the parse step into a new named function solely to make it unit-testable would itself be scope creep on a MINOR one-line bug fix -- adding production surface area (a new function signature) with no requirement or decision record calling for it, which is exactly what review checklist item 4 (scope creep) tells me to flag against, not encourage. The existing 22-test file plus the 3x N=16 concurrent-git repro (48 partition-runs, zero DateTime/lint_handoffs failures) already demonstrate the crash class is gone under the actual conditions that caused ISS-0412. TEST-DESIGNER's role on this handoff should be limited to a final regression-coverage sanity check: confirm test/mix/tasks/letflow.lint_handoffs_test.exs still covers the ARTIFACTS_OUT_SELF_REF warning's happy path (it should already, per the 22 passing tests) and that no coverage gap was introduced -- not author a new isolated unit test for the private parse branch and not perform the extract-for-testability refactor. If TEST-DESIGNER's own audit disagrees and wants the refactor, that is TEST-DESIGNER's call to make explicit and route through CODE-DESIGNER first (new function signature = design-notable), not something to do inline.
